clue.text: Brief commercial poll about early signs of consumer activity

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement

indicators.note: about means the poll word goes around the picked letters

parts.note: to poll is to vote, so poll gives VOTE

indicators.note: early signs means the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A short advertisement asks people about their first spending habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective for the commercial, but it is the noun: a brief is a barrister, a courtroom lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal slang a brief is a lawyer, and an advocate is one who pleads cases in court.

clue.text: Aim when facing pressure and anger

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
P is the physics symbol for pressure
ire means anger

explanation.surface: Someone takes aim while under strain and in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim high, or set one's sights on a goal, is to have ambitions.

clue.text: Free travel i.e. around Belgium? It's true

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the Belgium letter
free means the letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: Is free travel really available around Belgium?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges TRAVEL and IE into VERITALE, and 'around' wraps that round B.
explanation.definitionFit: Real or genuine, used to emphasise that a description is fully deserved.

clue.text: A class in creating courses?

parts.note: the courses are not of study but of a meal, so the class teaches how to prepare food

explanation.surface: It sounds like a seminar on designing curricula.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of preparing dishes for each stage of a meal is what such a class teaches.

clue.text: Characteristic element in extra item

indicators.note: element in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A distinctive feature turns up in an additional item.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguishing quality or feature of someone's personality is a characteristic.

clue.text: Circle that's disrupted minister

indicators.note: disrupted means the letters of the word circle are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A ring of people breaks apart, upsetting a government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a member of the clergy, the meaning of this noun.

clue.text: Take care in position on board

definitions.meaning: a warning to be careful, as in watch it
a crow's nest or watch post on a ship, a spot on board for keeping watch

explanation.surface: Be careful where you stand on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means beware; as a noun it is a watch station aboard ship.

clue.text: Skipper gracious describing big property?

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is something that skips and bounds
my and gracious are both mild exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A ship's captain, kindly, is talking about a large estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' wants to be a captain; it is a hopping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacious house has plenty of space inside, the word an estate agent would use for it.

clue.text: A lot of worry with time over musical work

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: concern means worry
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Plenty of anxiety and overtime goes into a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for solo instrument and orchestra is a classical musical work.

clue.text: Father upset mother perhaps? It's plain to see

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a mother is an example of a parent

explanation.surface: Dad is annoyed with Mum, and it shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious or evident is clearly visible to everyone.

clue.text: Sloppy on onerous PR plan? That could be it!

indicators.note: sloppy means careless or messy, so the letters of the four words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A careless publicity plan full of burdens is mocked as a likely failure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: the word 'it' in the clue is itself one of these grammatical words.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as it, he and she stand for nouns and refer to people or things: grammar's personal category.

clue.text: Losers might do this in place for contemplation

definitions.meaning: a beaten army falls back, withdrawing from the field
a quiet refuge where one goes for prayer or reflection

explanation.surface: Defeated people head off to somewhere quiet to think things over.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means withdraw after defeat; as a noun it is a secluded sanctuary for reflection.

clue.text: A line in shy note for trusty follower

indicators.note: in means the line letter goes inside the shy word

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bashful message sent to a loyal supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant at church services, and more widely a devoted attendant or disciple.

clue.text: A book with view about African party getting suspension

indicators.note: about means the view word wraps around the party

parts.note: to eye something is to view it
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's ruling party

explanation.surface: A book's account of an African political party sees it banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter held over, temporarily set aside and not in force, is in a state of suspension.

clue.text: Flier near pitch around the centre of Dijon

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: around means the pitch word goes round the middle letter

parts.note: pitch is tar, a black sticky substance

indicators.note: the centre of means the middle letter of the town's name

explanation.surface: A bird flies close to a sports ground in central Dijon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field, but here it is the black sticky substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal bird is a flier; flier is a crossword-favourite way to say bird.

clue.text: Entice interest emptying bottles

indicators.note: bottles means the phrase holds the answer inside it, as a bottle holds a drink

explanation.surface: Someone loses interest once the bottles have been drained.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or seduce someone into doing something is to entice them.

clue.text: Chaps get on trip taking day off to see animal sanctuary?

parts.note: chaps are men
to get on in years is to age

indicators.note: taking ... off means the day letter is removed from the trip word
off completes taking off, the instruction to remove the day letter

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: Men growing older take a trip, with a day off, to visit a wildlife park.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: a zoo-like collection of animals is not strictly a sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of wild animals kept in captivity for show, loosely a sanctuary for them.

clue.text: Lad hopes to move plant

indicators.note: to move means the letters of the two words are shifted into new places

explanation.surface: A boy hopes to relocate his home or business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory the lad is moving; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily of the Mediterranean, linked in legend with the Elysian fields, is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Material for Oxford perhaps moved around, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: swayed means moved from side to side

explanation.surface: Cloth from Oxford seems to have been shifted about, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the city or university, but here it is an oxford, a lace-up shoe, often made of brushed leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushed leather with a napped finish is a common material for smart lace-up shoes.

clue.text: Detective in audience witnessed ugly sight

parts.note: a private eye is a detective

indicators.note: in audience means heard by listeners, so the word counts by its sound

parts.note: saw means witnessed

explanation.surface: A detective among the onlookers saw something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech SAW and SORE are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpleasant to look at, an offence to the eye, such as a derelict building.

clue.text: Manage with others to wear medal

indicators.note: to wear means the medal goes around the other letters, as if worn over them

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or award
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: Someone copes in company by pinning on a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wear' casts the medal as a garment draped around the Latin abbreviation for and others.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope or get by somehow is to manage, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Imaginative famous songwriter almost restricted by unreliable ally

indicators.note: restricted by means the songwriter's letters are held inside the jumbled ally
unreliable means the letters of the word ally are not to be trusted in their order
almost means the last letter of the songwriter's name is dropped

parts.note: Tim Rice is the famous lyricist of Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar

explanation.surface: A creative songwriter is nearly held back by a treacherous partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The songwriter is Tim Rice, Andrew Lloyd Webber's lyricist; 'unreliable' scrambles the partner word so its letters fall either side of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic and expressive writing, full of feeling and imagination, is described this way.

clue.text: Ignore a ship in lead over year

indicators.note: over in a down clue means this part sits above the year letter
in means the ship letters sit inside the lead symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Ignore a vessel stuck in heavy metal for a year.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass someone by is to overlook or ignore them.

clue.text: Gather a lot of tough clothing to keep warm

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: hard means tough
a vest is an undergarment worn for warmth

explanation.surface: Collect plenty of hardwearing clothes to stay warm.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in or reap a crop is to gather it in.

clue.text: Quick criticism shown by papers?

parts.note: a rap is a sharp rebuke or criticism
ID is identification papers

explanation.surface: Swift criticism appears in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast or swift; quick is a straight synonym.

clue.text: American soldier seen in country area or Italian city

indicators.note: seen in means the soldier appears inside the other letters

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US soldier is spotted in a rural region or in an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital of Umbria, a hill city in central Italy.

clue.text: Leader in order, one interfering it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a pryer is a nosy person who interferes in others' affairs

explanation.surface: A head of something, someone who meddles, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is a religious order, not a command or sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk heading a religious house or ranking below an abbot leads a monastic community.

clue.text: MP spoilt accord I formulated for foreign officialdom

indicators.note: formulated means the letters of all four words are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A politician wrecks a treaty that he drew up, upsetting overseas officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: the indicator is 'formulated', which shuffles MP, SPOILT, ACCORD and I together.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of ambassadors and envoys posted to a country forms the foreign officials there.

clue.text: Doddery old German, temporary resident

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters totter into a new order

explanation.surface: A shaky elderly German is staying for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rents a room in another person's house is a short-term resident there.

clue.text: Titled figure in turn with early broadcast lacking a humorous quality

indicators.note: in turn means the noble's word is read backwards

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman with a title

indicators.note: broadcast scatters the letters of early, and lacking says the a is left out

explanation.surface: A nobleman turns up with an early-morning broadcast that has no charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast lacking' is a composite instruction: scatter the letters of the word and leave out the single A.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic oddness or whimsical humour; drollness is a near synonym.
